answer_1.quote: GRE uses a generative large language model (LLM) to extract relational triples from a source document D. The model functions on an autoregressive basis at the token level, expressed as P (x t |x 1 , x 2 , . . . , x t-1 , D), where x t represents the t th token in the output sequence.
answer_1.outputs: relation triples in the format [subject, relation, object]

answer_2.quote: To navigate these new dimensions, we introduce GENRES (GENerative Relation Extraction Scoring), a multi-dimensional framework tailored for evaluating GRE.

answer_3.quote: In this study, we adopt the approach from previous work and utilize an LLM as the fact-checking tool. Specifically, we employ GPT-3.5-Turbo-Instruct as the fact checker...

answer_4.quote: We further conducted human evaluation experiments to verify the alignment of our proposed GENRES with human preferences. Three annotators, who are all computer science graduate students, are involved in this evaluation.
